inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text:
This is really about who gets protected when politicians invoke “economic stability.” Defending gas-company profits and property-investor concessions while resisting calls for those with the most power to contribute more shifts the burden onto everyone else—even though families and businesses rely on strong public services and a fairer economy.

And the focus on Conservative unity risks eclipsing accountability. Hastie’s criticism of Trump and Taylor’s refusal to say whether he supports the US and Israel’s war with Iran raise serious questions. Voters deserve more than party discipline: they deserve leaders who are clear about whose interests their economic and international positions serve.
